channel.title: The Latin Wire
channel.description: Politics, business, entertainment, sports and culture for Hispanics

item.title: Carín León books three-night return to Las Vegas Sphere in 2027
item.description: The Hermosillo-born superstar is already heading back to the Sphere in September 2027, timed perfectly for Mexican Independence Day in Las Vegas.

item.title: Pumas host León in rescheduled Liga MX Apertura 2026 match
item.description: A Leagues Cup run pushed this Jornada 7 clash back four days; León arrives tired from the United States, Pumas from a two-goal loss.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks to bar armed ICE agents from 2026 polling places
item.description: A lawsuit over armed agents at polling places revives a tension as old as American democracy itself: who controls the ground around the vote?

item.title: Netflix marks 15 years in Mexico with $2.7 billion GDP contribution
item.description: The streaming giant says 15 years of local production added MXN$50 billion to GDP, with a fresh US$1 billion pledge through 2028.

item.title: Whitmer orders permit review, urges Enbridge to shut down Line 5
item.description: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer called on Enbridge CEO Gregory Ebel to shut down Line 5 within months as state regulators review tunnel permits.

item.title: Márquez begins Liga MX club tour as Mexico national team coach
item.description: The new El Tri boss kicked off visits to all 18 Liga MX clubs Tuesday, starting at Atlas, where his playing career began and ended.

item.title: DOJ and Education Dept. accuse UC Berkeley Law of racial bias in admissions
item.description: Federal agencies say the law school favored Black applicants over white and Asian applicants despite the Supreme Court's 2023 ban on race-conscious admissions.

item.title: China extends antidumping probe on Mexican pecan nuts six months
item.description: Beijing pushed back the deadline to March 2027, leaving tens of millions in Mexican pecan exports in limbo.

item.title: DiGenova resigns as head of DOJ probe into Trump foes
item.description: Joe diGenova confirmed his resignation to the Associated Press on Thursday, five months after taking over a Justice Department probe targeting former government officials.

item.title: U.S. third-country deportations draw scrutiny after cartel witness re-detained
item.description: A Mexican cartel witness deported to Guatemala and returned to Mexico has prompted legal challenges and renewed debate over U.S. third-country removal policies.

item.title: Vance urges Republicans to nationalize midterms at Dallas convention
item.description: The vice president told GOP leaders the party must remind voters of the administration's record and frame November's elections as a national referendum.

item.title: Kimmel moves Talarico interview to YouTube amid FCC pressure
item.description: ABC's Jimmy Kimmel moved a Thursday interview with Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to YouTube, citing FCC pressure on the network and its affiliates.

item.title: Harris to campaign with Ossoff in Georgia late October
item.description: Harris will keynote a Fulton County Democrats dinner and campaign alongside Ossoff, her expected final midterm stop, as other Democrats have declined her involvement.

item.title: Rafael Márquez officially presented as Mexico national team coach
item.description: The 47-year-old former captain takes charge of El Tri on September 10, targeting the Sports Project 2030 with a largely Spanish coaching staff.

item.title: Colombia's tourism sector earns $5.6 billion as earthquake recovery begins
item.description: Colombia's travel sector pulled in $5.6 billion in the first half of 2026, even as a deadly earthquake left 1.28 million people in need.

item.title: First Circuit upholds block on USPS mail ballot rule before midterms
item.description: A federal appeals court's mail ballot ruling reopens centuries-old tensions over who actually controls American elections.

item.title: James Rodríguez agrees verbal deal to join Atlético Nacional
item.description: The 34-year-old free agent has a verbal deal worth 1.2 million euros per year, with a registration deadline of September 11 looming.

item.title: IMF says rising Argentine household delinquency poses no financial risk
item.description: The IMF says Argentine bank buffers are solid despite a record 5.8 million borrowers falling 90-plus days behind on payments.

item.title: Trump administration proposes ending 60-day H-1B grace period
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security published a proposed rule that would require H-1B and other work visa holders to leave the United States immediately upon losing their jobs.

item.title: Atlas signs Elías Montiel from Pachuca for record $12 million
item.description: Atlas FC paid a club-record $12 million for 80 percent of Elías Montiel's rights, with $3 million more possible in performance bonuses.

item.title: Chile submits capital market reform bill as central bank holds rates
item.description: Chile's MK4 bill targets savings, startups, and foreign capital while the central bank holds its benchmark rate at 4.50%.

item.title: DHS leaves El Salvador TPS status unresolved as deadline passes
item.description: DHS missed a statutory deadline and offered no ruling as El Salvador's TPS designation lapsed, leaving roughly 170,000 to 200,000 Salvadorans in legal limbo.

item.title: Reports show Latino electorate growing and politically dealigning ahead of midterms
item.description: Pew and AS/COA data show Latino eligible voters reaching 36 million, with party loyalty eroding on both sides ahead of November.

item.title: Optimum opens 19th annual Hispanic Heritage Essay Contest for students
item.description: Optimum's 19th annual Hispanic Heritage Essay Contest invites middle and high schoolers to explore Hispanic culture for a shot at a $3,000 scholarship.

item.title: Tigres officially signs striker Guillermo 'Memote' Martínez from Pumas
item.description: Tigres pays $1.3 million to land the 31-year-old Mexican international as a last-minute addition to fill a gaping hole up front.

item.title: Supreme Court again blocks Missouri's new GOP congressional map
item.description: Missouri's congressional map fight reveals a deeper, unresolved tension between federal and state authority over federal elections.

item.title: New York Latino Film Festival opens its 26th edition in September
item.description: The New York Latino Film Festival returns September 15–20, 2026, bringing over 125 films from 20 countries to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month.

item.title: Mexican striker Julián Quiñones nominated for Ballon d'Or 2026
item.description: Quiñones lands a Ballon d'Or nomination for the first time in 19 years for a Mexican player, backed by 41 goals and a strong World Cup.

item.title: MoneyGram launches stablecoin Visa card first in Colombia
item.description: MoneyGram's stablecoin Visa card goes live in Colombia first, letting users hold dollar balances and spend where Visa is accepted.

item.title: Trump pledges $5,000 dividend to adults if Republicans win midterms
item.description: Trump told supporters at a Dallas convention that every adult citizen would receive $5,000 if Republicans hold Congress in November.

item.title: Nubank enters US market with savings account, credit card, and remittances
item.description: Nu Holdings launches a no-fee credit card, a 3.50% APY savings account, and fee-free remittances to three countries on September 10, 2026.

item.title: Petrobras extends natural gas supply deal with Braskem to 2029
item.description: Braskem's gas supply deal with Petrobras grows to BRL 1.85 billion and runs three years longer than originally planned.

item.title: 9/11's 25th anniversary splits parties on war, memory, and security powers
item.description: The 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks is dividing both parties on questions of memory, national security powers, and the Iran war.

item.title: Republicans hold first-ever midterm convention in Dallas
item.description: The Republican National Committee convened in Dallas for what it called the first midterm convention in modern American political history.

item.title: Turning Point USA marks one year since Charlie Kirk's assassination
item.description: Turning Point USA marked one year since Charlie Kirk's fatal shooting with a memorial at Utah Valley University as his trial moves forward.

item.title: Trump promises $500 ACA rebate checks to 1 million enrollees
item.description: President Trump pledged $500 checks to roughly 1 million ACA enrollees in 30 states, citing what he called a Biden-era surplus of exchange user fees.

item.title: De Paul taunts Lewandowski with World Cup record in MLS draw
item.description: De Paul invoked his two Copa Américas and a World Cup to silence Lewandowski after a late scuffle at Soldier Field.

item.title: Petrobras corrects gasoline price after Brazil cuts fuel taxes
item.description: A midnight correction untangled two identical R$0.63 figures that briefly made it look like a tax cut and a price hike cancelled each other out.

item.title: 9/11 25th anniversary marked by new museum exhibition and illness toll
item.description: As the 25th anniversary arrives, the death toll keeps climbing and a trove of newly released documents raises enduring questions about what officials knew.

item.title: GOP courts Hispanic voters at Dallas convention as Texas polls tighten
item.description: Republicans gathered in Dallas to make their case to Hispanic voters as new polling shows Democratic candidates competitive across Texas.
